Page number and gathering mark at the foot right. The narrow strip at the left edge is the neighbouring page's margin and is not transcribed.

l.i: Mucrone nudo dexteram armat, at manum
Bilance laevam: hâc ponderat legum vices,
Illo at, seuerè probra cuncta demetit.
O ter beatos, sacra queis aenigmata
Iuris patent! mortalitatis hi parum
Habent, Diis sed proximi immortalibus,
Post fata, cæli possidebunt culmina.
Adscripsit huicce casta Te quoque ordini
STEKI Themis; quam vindicare laus tibi
Est unica; id quod ore, scriptis, comprobas.
Nomen vetustas sic teret nunquam tuum,
Virtus quod astris inserit micantibus.
ET Themis, & Pallas de digno anademate
certat, Utraque prima tuas vult redimisse comas.
Illa canit sanctos Legum in mysteria amores;
Hæc Aristotelica prædicat artis opes.
Scande alacris Pindum, & varii magnalia Juris
Explica, Hyanthei buccina grata chori.
Ista tui ingenii magmenta Jehova secundet,
Teq; subinde suâ pro bonitate juvet.
Eja age fac quæ te Charites facere usque sorores
Urgent, hisce tibi est vita colenda modis.

page.notes: The left strip shows the margin of the neighbouring page (fragments such as "IC.", "aberrat", "Lucius", "Mucro"); it is not transcribed. Two ornamental rules and a decorative initial "E" are not text. The word "anademate" and "ænigmata" are read from a difficult italic and may be inexact; "magmenta" is as printed.
